title_en: Guangdong Yellow River Industrial Group Co., Ltd. v. Beijing Ranzi Traditional Chinese Medicine Science and Technology Development Center — dispute over infringement of equity transfer
ruling_gist_en: A natural person who serves as the legal representative of a legal person, in the name of that legal person, fraudulently enters into a civil contract with another party, whereby the property obtained is possessed by the legal person. The legal consequence arising therefrom is that the natural person is suspected of committing the crime of contract fraud, while a creditor-debt relationship is formed between the legal person and the other party due to the rescission of the contract. The people's court shall, in accordance with Article 10 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes, transfer the part of the case involving the natural person's suspected crime to the public security organs for handling, and continue to try the civil dispute part.
keywords_en: civil; equity transfer infringement dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; Guangdong; legal person; Contract Law; Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases Involving Suspected Economic Crimes; whether the equity transfer contract is revocable due to fraud; whether suspected economic crime and civil dispute should be tried separately; affirm the original judgment; equity transfer; fraud; false identity; project development right; good faith; deception; central general equity transfer infringement dispute
full_text_en:
Guangdong Yellow River Industrial Group Co., Ltd. v.
Beijing Ranzi Traditional Chinese Medicine Technology Development Center
— dispute over general equity transfer infringement

【Ruling Summary】

Where a natural person who serves as the legal representative of a legal person, in the name of that legal person, uses fraudulent means to enter into a civil contract with another person, and the property obtained thereby is taken into possession by the legal person, the legal consequences are that the natural person is suspected of the crime of contract fraud, and at the same time a creditor-debtor relationship arises between the legal person and the other person as a result of the contract being revoked. The people's court shall, in accordance with Article 10 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Economic Disputes Involving Economic Criminal Suspicions, transfer the part involving the natural person's suspected crime to the public security organ for handling, while continuing to hear the civil dispute part.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 62

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Beijing Ranzi Traditional Chinese Medicine Technology Development Center, domiciled at Room 516, No. 18 Fukang Road, Science and Technology Park, Changping District, Beijing.
Legal Representative: Liu Xianqi, General Manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Song Yanlu, lawyer of Beijing Zhongyida Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Cai Chunyu, lawyer of Beijing Zhongyida Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Guangdong Yellow River Industrial Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 8, 7th Floor, Yellow River Commercial City, Gangkou Road, Humen Town, Dongguan City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Zheng Qianghui, Chairman of the company.
Agent ad litem: Song Yanjun, Manager of the company.
Agent ad litem: Bie Jinsong, lawyer of Beijing Huayi Law Firm.

The appellant Beijing Ranzi Traditional Chinese Medicine Technology Development Center (hereinafter referred to as Ranzi Center) appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2007) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 773 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of general equity transfer infringement dispute with the appellee Guangdong Yellow River Industrial Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yellow River Company). This Court formed a collegial panel composed of presiding judge Jin Jianfeng, acting judges Yin Yuan and Pan Yongfeng to hear the case, with Bai Xue serving as the clerk. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The Beijing High People's Court found the following facts: Beijing Xiannongtan Medical Science City Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiannongtan Company) was established in April 2003, with Liu Xianqi as its legal representative, and a registered capital of RMB 50,000,000. Its shareholders were: Ranzi Center contributing RMB 30,000,000, accounting for 60% of the registered capital; Huludao Yinhe Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. contributing RMB 20,000,000, accounting for 40% of the registered capital.

In December 2004, Huludao Yinhe Economic and Trade Co., Ltd. transferred its shares of RMB 20,000,000 in Xiannongtan Company to Beijing Jiangshan Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiangshan Company). The amended equity structure of Xiannongtan Company was: Ranzi Center contributing RMB 30,000,000, accounting for 60% of the registered capital; Jiangshan Company contributing RMB 20,000,000, accounting for 40% of the registered capital. Ranzi Center is a joint stock cooperative enterprise with a registered capital of RMB 2,880,000 and its legal representative is Liu Xianqi.

On November 19, 20, and 21, 2006, Ranzi Center, Jiangshan Company, and Xiannongtan Company successively passed shareholders' resolutions, the main contents of which were: 1. All shareholders agreed that the 60% equity interest held by Ranzi Center in Xiannongtan Company should be transferred to Yellow River Company; 2. Jiangshan Company waived its preemptive right to purchase the equity; 3. After the equity transfer, Jiangshan Company was to assume all debts and credits of Xiannongtan Company before the equity transfer.

On November 22, 2006, Ranzi Center and Yellow River Company signed an Equity Transfer Agreement, stipulating: 1. Ranzi Center would transfer its 60% equity interest in Xiannongtan Company to Yellow River Company at a price of RMB 260,000,000; 2. Yellow River Company would pay a deposit of RMB 10,000,000 within 3 days after signing the Agreement, RMB 90,000,000 before December 30, 2006, RMB 60,000,000 before June 30, 2007, and RMB 100,000,000 before December 31, 2007; 3. Ranzi Center would start assisting with the change of the register of shareholders after receiving all the transfer price from Yellow River Company, and from the date of such change, Yellow River Company would become a shareholder of Xiannongtan Company; 4. Liquidated damages: Yellow River Company would pay Ranzi Center a late payment penalty of 1% for each day of delay in payment, and Ranzi Center had the right to terminate the Agreement, and Yellow River Company would bear liquidated damages of 2% of the share transfer price.

The Equity Transfer Agreement was accompanied by 14 appendices. According to the contents of the appendices: In 2002, the Traditional Chinese Medicine Professional Committee under the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee (hereinafter referred to as the TCM Professional Committee) signed an agreement with the People's Government of Xuanwu District, Beijing, stipulating that the TCM Professional Committee would establish the "Beijing Xiannongtan International Science and Medical City" in Xuanwu District. On March 18, 2003, the TCM Professional Committee decided to establish the "Beijing Xiannongtan Medical Science City" and accordingly set up Xiannongtan Company. This plan was later not realized. In March 2005, the TCM Professional Committee signed an agreement with the People's Government of Dachang Hui Autonomous County, Hebei Province (hereinafter referred to as Dachang County Government), stipulating that the TCM Professional Committee would establish the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City in Dachang County, with a total investment of RMB 21.5 billion, to be constructed over a period of 6 years in three phases. The first phase required an investment of RMB 3 billion over a period of two years. If no significant progress was made within two years, the agreement would be terminated automatically. Later, upon application by the Dachang County Government, the Standing Committee of the Dachang County People's Congress approved the "Planning Scheme for the Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City," and the planned area for the project was 46,800 mu.

On November 24, 2006, after Ranzi Center and Yellow River Company signed the agreement, Yellow River Company transferred the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 into Ranzi Center's account. Thereafter, Yellow River Company, believing that Liu Xianqi was suspected of fraud, reported the case to the Chaoyang Branch of the Beijing Public Security Bureau (hereinafter referred to as Chaoyang Public Security Bureau), and froze the RMB 10,000,000 equity transfer payment through the China Banking Regulatory Commission. Yellow River Company did not pay the remaining equity transfer price, and the parties did not complete the procedures for changing the register of shareholders.

During the trial of this case, because Liu Xianqi, the legal representative of Ranzi Center in this case, was suspected of committing a crime, the collegial panel of this Court hearing the case investigated the relevant circumstances with the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau. The Chaoyang Public Security Bureau stated that, when the parties signed the agreement, Liu Xianqi claimed that his current identity was the Director of the Bureau of Retired Cadres of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China, and had previously served as the Commander of the 54th Group Army, the Commander of the Shanghai Garrison Command, and the Commander of the Hunan Provincial Military Command. He also claimed that he had the primary development rights for 46,800 mu of land in Dachang County, to be used for developing the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City, and that the previous five-year plan of the National Development and Reform Commission had already included a plan for it, which had been approved and filed, including approval by the Ministry of Land and Resources. As long as the land transfer fee was paid, primary development could be carried out. Liu Xianqi also claimed that because of his special identity, he could not directly sell the project, but it could be achieved through an equity transfer. That is, Xiannongtan Company was the only enterprise that could develop the Science City. If Yellow River Company purchased Ranzi Center's 60% equity in Xiannongtan Company, Yellow River Company would own 60% of Xiannongtan Company's equity, become the majority shareholder of Xiannongtan Company, control Xiannongtan Company, and thus effectively obtain the primary development rights for the project land. Yellow River Company asked Liu Xianqi to produce the approval documents from the National Development and Reform Commission for the project establishment and the documents from the land department. Liu Xianqi deceived Yellow River Company into trusting him by using false reasons, and the parties signed the Equity Transfer Agreement. That is, Yellow River Company signed the contract without seeing any national-level approval documents. After Yellow River Company paid the RMB 10,000,000 equity transfer payment to Ranzi Center, Yellow River Company proposed to jointly manage the RMB 10,000,000 with Liu Xianqi, which Liu Xianqi refused, arousing Yellow River Company's suspicion. Later, Yellow River Company learned that the Director of the Bureau of Retired Cadres of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China was not Liu Xianqi, and reported the case to the public security organ.

On November 26, 2006, the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau decided to file a case and investigate Liu Xianqi for fraud. On November 27 of the same year, Liu Xianqi was detained. On December 30 of the same year, Liu Xianqi was released on bail pending trial. On August 6, 2007, the Beijing Chaoyang District People's Procuratorate approved Liu Xianqi's arrest on suspicion of fraud.

To verify the authenticity of Liu Xianqi's identity, the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau conducted investigations with relevant departments and confirmed that all the various identities Liu Xianqi had claimed were false. The materials obtained included a certificate issued by the Second Appointment and Removal Bureau of the Cadre Department of the General Political Department of the People's Liberation Army to the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau on June 1, 2007, stating that, upon investigation, there was no such person as Liu Xianqi among the successive cadres at the military and division levels of the 54th Group Army, the Shanghai Garrison Command, and the Hunan Provincial Military Command.

To verify the authenticity of the project, the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau conducted investigations with relevant departments. The materials showed: 1. On November 28, 2006, the State Administration of Public Institutions Registration issued a Certificate stating: Upon investigation, the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee and the Traditional Chinese Medicine Professional Committee under the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee had not registered as legal persons of public institutions with this Administration. 2. The Archives of the Ministry of Civil Affairs issued five Certificates on June 1, 2007, stating that the six names appearing in the case — "National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee," "CHC National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee," "Traditional Chinese Medicine Professional Committee under the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee," "CHC Traditional Chinese Medicine Professional Committee under the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee," "National High-tech Industrialization Cooperation Organization," and "National High-tech Industrialization Cooperation Consortium" — had not been registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs.

To verify the authenticity of the land development claimed by Liu Xianqi, the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau visited the National Development and Reform Commission, which stated that there was no such project establishment approval; visited the Ministry of Land and Resources, which replied that there was no such project establishment; visited the Hebei Provincial Department of Land and Resources, which replied that there was no such application, because land use over 500 mu must be submitted to the State Council for approval; visited the Dachang County Government of Hebei Province, which replied that they did not deny having a person like Liu Xianqi, but had clearly informed him that he must handle the development procedures himself. The Dachang County People's Congress had issued a document agreeing with Liu Xianqi's idea, but would not handle the procedures. This project had not even been reported to Langfang City, Hebei Province.

On April 3, 2007, the Dachang County Government issued a letter to the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee, "Regarding the Termination of the Agreement on Cooperation in Building the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City," which stated: We have received your documents No. (2007)03 and No. (2007)11. According to Article 5 of the "Agreement on Cooperation in Building the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City" signed by both parties on March 30, 2005: The total investment for the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City project under this agreement is RMB 21.5 billion, with a construction period of 6 years divided into three phases (each phase 2 years). The first phase requires an investment of RMB 3 billion, with a construction period of 2 years. If no significant progress is made within 2 years, the agreement will be terminated automatically. In view of the fact that your side has not fulfilled the relevant obligations under the agreement, including investment and construction, as agreed, upon study, the "Agreement on Cooperation in Building the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City" signed by both parties on March 30, 2005, is terminated automatically.

On April 17, 2007, the Dachang County Government issued a Certificate to the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau, stating: (1) The "Agreement on Cooperation in Building the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City" signed by the Dachang County Government and the TCM Professional Committee on March 30, 2005, has been terminated automatically, and the National High-tech Health Industry Working Committee has been notified by letter; (2) After the two parties signed the "Agreement on Cooperation in Building the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City," only the Standing Committee of the County People's Congress approved the "Planning Scheme for the Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City." By the end of 2006, because the project did not yet meet the conditions for applying for project establishment, no application for project establishment had been made, and it had not been approved by relevant higher authorities; (3) The TCM Professional Committee had not obtained the land use rights within the project planning area. Relying solely on the "Planning Scheme for the Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City" approved by the Standing Committee of our County People's Congress, development and construction could not proceed.

Through the above investigations, the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau confirmed that Liu Xianqi had fabricated his identity and facts when he signed the Equity Transfer Agreement on behalf of Ranzi Center with Yellow River Company.

On April 18, 2007, Ranzi Center filed a lawsuit with the Beijing High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering Yellow River Company to pay the equity transfer price of RMB 90,000,000 and late payment penalties of RMB 97,200,000. On October 30, 2007, Yellow River Company filed a counterclaim against Ranzi Center, requesting: 1. Revocation of the equity transfer agreement signed by both parties; 2. An order that Ranzi Center return the RMB 10,000,000 to it and pay liquidated damages of RMB 804,000 (during the trial, after clarification by the court, Yellow River Company's claim for liquidated damages was specified as a claim for interest, calculated according to the enterprise deposit interest rate for the same period until the date of payment); 3. Litigation costs to be borne by Ranzi Center. On December 10, 2007, Ranzi Center applied to withdraw its lawsuit against Yellow River Company, and the Beijing High People's Court ruled to permit Ranzi Center to withdraw the lawsuit.

The Beijing High People's Court held that Ranzi Center is one of the parties in this case. Liu Xianqi, as its legal representative, was suspected of fraud in connection with the equity transfer in this case, and had been approved for arrest by the procuratorial authority and placed on the national wanted list. Article 10 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Economic Disputes Involving Economic Criminal Suspicions stipulates: "If, during the trial of economic dispute cases, a people's court discovers clues or materials of economic criminal suspicion that are related to the case but do not constitute the same legal relationship, it shall transfer the criminal suspicion clues or materials to the relevant public security or procuratorial organs for investigation and handling, and continue the trial of the economic dispute case." According to the above provision, as to the part concerning Liu Xianqi's suspected crime in this case, this court will deliver the relevant case file materials to the Chaoyang Public Security Bureau, which does not affect the trial of the civil part concerning the equity transfer between Ranzi Center and Yellow River Company in this case.

Based on the existing evidence, it can be proven that before the Equity Transfer Agreement was signed between Ranzi Center and Yellow River Company on November 22, 2006, Liu Xianqi, the legal representative of Ranzi Center, fabricated a special identity and the fact that he had the primary development rights for the land. Using fraudulent means, he caused Yellow River Company to mistakenly believe the falsehoods, to make an erroneous expression of intent, and to sign the agreement against its true intention. When the parties signed the agreement, Yellow River Company's purpose was to obtain the development rights for the 46,800 mu of land. The transfer was at a price higher than the value of the transferred equity, and the appendices to the agreement already reflected the development of the China Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City within Dachang County. This shows that the true purpose of the equity transfer agreement was to obtain the so-called primary development rights for the 46,800 mu of land. However, in fact, Ranzi Center did not have such land development rights. Liu Xianqi, using a false identity and fraudulent means, deceived Yellow River Company into trusting him and signed the agreement, thereby enabling Ranzi Center to obtain RMB 10,000,000 in equity transfer payments from Yellow River Company.

Article 54, paragraph 2, of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If a contract is concluded by one party through fraud or duress, or by taking advantage of the other party's hardship, causing the other party to express an intention against its true will, the injured party has the right to request the people's court or an arbitration institution to modify or revoke the contract." According to this provision, the nature of the Equity Transfer Agreement signed by both parties in this case should be determined as a voidable contract. Yellow River Company delivered a deposit of RMB 10,000,000 to Ranzi Center based on this agreement and is the injured party. Yellow River Company has the right, within the period for exercising the right of revocation, to request the people's court to revoke the agreement and to request Ranzi Center, as the infringing party, to return the deposit of RMB 10,000,000 and compensate for losses. Since a voidable contract has no legal binding force from the beginning, Ranzi Center must return the RMB 10,000,000 equity transfer payment it has received from Yellow River Company to Yellow River Company and compensate Yellow River Company for its losses. Yellow River Company's request for revocation of the contract and return of the equity transfer payment is supported. Since the contract between the parties is revoked, there is no issue of breach of contract. Therefore, Yellow River Company's change of its claim for liquidated damages to a claim for interest loss during the trial is in accordance with the law and is supported. As to the issue of Liu Xianqi's suspected economic crime, this court will transfer the case file materials concerning the suspected crime to the public security organ in accordance with the law, which does not affect the trial and judgment of the civil part of this case. In summary, pursuant to Articles 54, 55, and 58 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby orders:

1. Revocation of the Equity Transfer Agreement signed between Ranzi Center and Yellow River Company on November 22, 2006;
2. Ranzi Center shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, return to Yellow River Company the equity transfer payment of RMB 10,000,000 and compensate for the corresponding interest (calculated according to the enterprise deposit interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, from November 24, 2006 to the date of full payment).

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 43,312, to be borne by Ranzi Center.

Ranzi Center, dissatisfied with the original judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this court, alleging that: (1) The original judgment found that Liu Xianqi had committed fraud based on the investigative materials of the Chaoyang Public Security Sub-bureau and the transcripts of conversations with the handling police officers, which constituted insufficient evidence for the determination of facts. As to the authenticity of the project, the materials provided by the Chaoyang Public Security Sub-bureau to the court of first instance regarding the registration status of the National High-Tech Health Industry Working Committee and other entities had no relevance to this case. In this regard, Ranzi Center had submitted relevant evidence, and since some of that evidence consisted of official documents kept by state organs, it requested the court to retrieve the original evidence. The court of first instance did not conduct investigation and evidence collection, nor did it organize cross-examination of the evidence already submitted, and it lacked sufficient evidence to determine that the project lacked authenticity based solely on evidence lacking relevance. The National High-Tech Industrialization Collaborative Organization is a collaborative organization jointly established by nine ministries, including the Ministry of Information Industry, or their subordinate departments, aimed at promoting the industrialization of science and technology; by its nature, it is neither an enterprise, nor a social organization, nor a state organ or public institution; therefore, it is certainly impossible for the corresponding registration authority to have registration materials for the entities involved in this case. The Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City project involved in the case did indeed exist, and the progress of project development and whether the project exists are two different matters. The letter and certificate issued by the Dachang County Government proved that this project truly existed and that effective development work had been carried out. The key to determining whether fraud was established lies in whether the project existed at the time the contract was signed, whereas various circumstances arising during the performance of the contract that caused slow progress or abandonment all fall within normal commercial risks. Huanghe Company's acquisition of Ranzi Center's shares in Xiannongtan Company may have been based on the optimistic prospects of the traditional Chinese medicine industry or other considerations; the price for the equity transfer, as negotiated between the parties, did not involve any intention to purchase 46,800 mu of land for RMB 260 million. Huanghe Company's contractual purpose was to obtain Ranzi Center's equity in Xiannongtan Company, and obtaining the land development rights was merely a motive. The original judgment's determination of Huanghe Company's contractual purpose violates the principles of contract law and is unjust. (2) The original judgment found that Liu Xianqi, as the legal representative of Ranzi Center, had fabricated facts when signing the equity transfer contract with Huanghe Company, constituting fraud. This is not only based on the same legal relationship as the criminal suspicion found by the public security authorities, but also constitutes the same act as the fraudulent act found by the public security authorities. Therefore, the original judgment is self-contradictory, and its reliance on the investigative materials of the public security authorities and the application of Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crime Suspects in the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases manifestly constitutes an error in the application of law. In this case, the principal claim involves criminal suspicion, whereas the counterclaim does not fall within the same legal relationship as the criminal suspicion, and the use of criminal materials to decide the case deprives Ranzi Center of its procedural rights and harms its lawful rights and interests. Ranzi Center requests that the original judgment be set aside and that Huanghe Company's lawsuit be dismissed by ruling.

Huanghe Company, the appellee, argued in its defense: According to the facts determined by the court of first instance during the trial, Liu Xianqi, the legal representative of Ranzi Center, assumed a false identity, fabricated the Traditional Chinese Medicine Science City project and the fact that it had obtained the primary development rights for 46,800 mu of land, thereby defrauding Huanghe Company's trust, and signed the Equity Transfer Agreement in the form of a contract, thereby defrauding the first tranche of funds of RMB 10 million, causing huge economic losses. The facts prove that Ranzi Center neither had nor could obtain the primary development rights for 46,800 mu of land. Since the Equity Transfer Agreement was signed when Huanghe Company was deceived and its true intent was not reflected, the original judgment revoking that agreement was based on clear factual findings and correct application of law. Huanghe Company requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

After trial in the second instance, this court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

Opinion of the Court: Huanghe Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, seeking to rescind the Equity Transfer Agreement it had signed with Ranzi Center, on the grounds that the agreement was induced by fraud by Liu Xianqi, the legal representative of Ranzi Center, and was contrary to Huanghe Company's true intent. To ascertain this fact, the court of first instance conducted an investigation with the Chaoyang Public Security Sub-bureau, which was investigating Liu Xianqi for suspected crimes. Based on Liu Xianqi's confession and investigations of relevant departments, the Chaoyang Public Security Sub-bureau confirmed that when Liu Xianqi signed the Equity Transfer Agreement with Huanghe Company on behalf of Ranzi Center, he had assumed a false identity and fabricated facts. The court of first instance, based on the existing evidence, made a determination that Liu Xianqi, using a false identity and fraudulent means, defrauded Huanghe Company's trust, signed the agreement, and caused Ranzi Center to obtain RMB 10 million in equity transfer payments from Huanghe Company. This determination was not improper. Ranzi Center's appeal asserts that the facts of the case were determined with insufficient evidence, but it cannot provide evidence to negate the above facts. Therefore, its appeal arguments cannot stand, and this court does not support them.

According to the facts ascertained in this case, Liu Xianqi, as the legal representative of Ranzi Center, used fraudulent means in the name of Ranzi Center to sign a civil contract with Huanghe Company, and the funds obtained were possessed by Ranzi Center. The legal consequence of the above facts is that, in addition to Liu Xianqi's personal suspicion of fraud, a creditor-debtor relationship was formed between Ranzi Center and Huanghe Company due to the revocation of the contract, and Ranzi Center should bear corresponding civil liability in accordance with the law. Therefore, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 10 of this court's Provisions on Certain Issues Concerning the Handling of Economic Crime Suspects in the Trial of Economic Dispute Cases, transferred the part involving Liu Xianqi's suspected crime to the public security authorities, while continuing to hear the civil dispute part of this case. This was not improper, and this court affirms it. Ranzi Center's appeal ground that the case and the criminal suspicion found by the public security authorities are based on the same legal relationship and that Huanghe Company's lawsuit should be dismissed by ruling has no legal basis, and this court does not support it.

In summary, the appeal grounds of Ranzi Center have no factual or legal basis. The original judgment had clear factual findings and correct application of law and should be affirmed. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court renders the following judgment:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 43,312 shall be borne by Beijing Ranzi Traditional Chinese Medicine Science and Technology Development Center.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jin Jianfeng

Acting Judge: Yin Yuan

Acting Judge: Pan Yongfeng

April 22, 2008

Clerk: Bai Xue

[Profile of the Presiding Judge]

Jin Jianfeng (Senior Judge): Born in 1959, Doctor of Laws, appointed as a judge of the Supreme People's Court in 1998.
